The unit vector along the vector $\vec{a}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{\imath}+\hat{\jmath}+\hat{k})$
$\vec{a}=5(\hat{\imath}+\hat{\jmath}+\hat{k})$

Its direction ratios are.

questions.q: The x -coordinate of a point on the line joining the points $\mathrm{P}(2,2,1)$ and $Q(5,1,-2)$ is 4 . Find its $z$-coordinate.
questions.solution:
Equation of line PQ is $\frac{\mathrm{x}-2}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-2}{-1}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-1}{-3}$
Any point on the line is $(3 \lambda+2,-\lambda+2,-3 \lambda+1)$
$3 \lambda+2=4 \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{2}{3} \quad \therefore z \text { coord. }=-3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+1=-1 .$

Let $\mathrm{R}(4, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z})$ lying on PQ divides PQ in the ratio $\mathrm{k}: 1$
$\Rightarrow 4=\frac{5 \mathrm{k}+2}{\mathrm{k}+1} \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=2$
$\therefore z=\frac{2(-2)+1(1)}{2+1}=\frac{-3}{3}=-1$

questions.q: Find the distance of the point $(-1,-5,-10)$ from the point of intersection of the lines $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{3}=\frac{z-3}{4}$ and $\frac{x-4}{5}=\frac{y-1}{2}=z$.
questions.solution:
$l_1: \frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{3}=\frac{z-3}{4}=\lambda$
Any point on $l_1$ is $(2 \lambda+1,3 \lambda+2,4 \lambda+3)$
$l_2: \frac{x-4}{5}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z-0}{1}=\mu$
Any point on $l_2$ is $(5 \mu+4,2 \mu+1, \mu)$
For point of intersection,
$2 \lambda+1=5 \mu+4,3 \lambda+2=2 \mu+1$
Solving, $\lambda=\mu=-1$
Since, $\lambda=\mu=-1$ satisfy $4 \lambda+3=\mu$
$\therefore$ Point of intersection is $(-1,-1,-1)$
Now distance of $(-1,-5,-10)$ from $(-1,-1,-1)$ is:
$\sqrt{(-1+1)^2+(-1+5)^2+(-1+10)^2}=\sqrt{97} \text { units }$

questions.solution:
Let, $\vec{a}_1=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}, \vec{a}_2=4 \hat{i}+\hat{j}$
$\vec{b}_1=2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}, \vec{b}_2=5 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+\hat{k}$
$\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1=3 \hat{i}-\hat{j}-3 \hat{k}$
$\overrightarrow{b_1} \times \vec{b}_2=-5 \hat{i}+18 \hat{j}-11 \hat{k}$
Here, $\left(\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1\right) \cdot\left(\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2\right)=-15-18+33=0$
Hence given lines are not skew lines.

questions.q: Let the polished side of the mirror be along the line $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{1-y}{-2}=\frac{2 z-4}{6}$. A point $\mathrm{P}(1,6,3)$, some distance away from the mirror, has its image formed behind the mirror. Find the coordinates of the image point and the distance between the point $P$ and its image.
questions.solution:
Equation of given line is $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{3}$
Let coordinates of point on the line be $(\lambda, 2 \lambda+1,3 \lambda+2)$ for some $\lambda$
Drs of line perpendicular to line along mirror are $<\lambda-1,2 \lambda-5,3 \lambda-1> (\lambda-1) \cdot 1+(2 \lambda-5) \cdot 2+(3 \lambda-1) \cdot 3=0$ gives $\lambda=1$
Coordinates of foot of perpendicular are $(1,3,5)$
For image
$\frac{x+1}{2}=1, \frac{y+6}{2}=3, \frac{z+3}{2}=5 \text { gives image as }(1,0,7)$
Required distance $=\sqrt{0+36+16}=2 \sqrt{13}$

questions.q: Find the image of the point $(-1,5,2)$ in the line $\frac{2 \mathrm{x}-4}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{y}}{2}=\frac{2-\mathrm{z}}{3}$. Find the length of the line segment joining the points (given point and the image point).
questions.solution:
Let $A^{\prime}(a, b, c)$ be the image of the point $A(-1,5,2)$ in the given line, also assume ' $M$ ' as the point of intersection of $A A^{\prime}$ with the given line, then ' $M$ ' is the mid-point of the line segment $\mathbf{A A}^{\prime}$

The Line in the standard form is: $\frac{x-2}{1}=\frac{y}{2}=\frac{z-2}{-3}$, then
$M$ is the point $(\lambda+2,2 \lambda,-3 \lambda+2)$, for some $\lambda \in R$
Direction Ratios of AM are $\lambda+3,2 \lambda-5,-3 \lambda$
$\mathrm{AM} \perp \mathrm{Line}, \therefore 1(\lambda+3)+2(2 \lambda-5)-3(-3 \lambda)=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{1}{2}$
$M\left(\frac{5}{2}, 1, \frac{1}{2}\right)=M\left(\frac{a-1}{2}, \frac{b+5}{2}, \frac{c+2}{2}\right) \Rightarrow a=6, b=-3, c=-1$
$\therefore$ The Image of A in the line is $\mathrm{A}^{\prime}(6,-3,-1)$
And, $A A^{\prime}=\sqrt{49+64+9}=\sqrt{122}$

questions.q: Find the image $\mathrm{A}^{\prime}$ of the point $\mathrm{A}(1,6,3)$ in the line $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-2}{3}$. Also, find the equation of the line joining A and $\mathrm{A}^{\prime}$.
questions.solution:
The equation of given line is $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{3}=\lambda$
Any arbitrary point on the line is $M(\lambda, 2 \lambda+1,3 \lambda+2)$
dr's of $A M$ are $<\lambda-1,2 \lambda-5,3 \lambda-1>$
$\operatorname{Here} 1(\lambda-1)+2(2 \lambda-5)+3(3 \lambda-1)=0$
$\Rightarrow \lambda=1$
$\therefore M(1,3,5)$ is the foot perpendicular of the point A to the given line.
Let image of point A in the line be $A^{\prime}(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$
Since $M$ is the mid-point of $A A^{\prime}, \operatorname{so} M\left(\frac{1+\alpha}{2}, \frac{6+\beta}{2}, \frac{3+\gamma}{2}\right)=M(1,3,5) \Rightarrow A^{\prime}(1,0,7)$ is the image of A .
Also, Equation of $A A^{\prime}$ is $\frac{x-1}{0}=\frac{y-6}{-3}=\frac{z-3}{2}$
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Find a point P on the line $\frac{x+5}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}+3}{4}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-6}{-9}$ such that its distance from point $\mathrm{Q}(2,4,-1)$ is 7 units. Also, find the equation of line joining $P$ and $Q$.
questions.solution:
The given line is $\frac{x+5}{1}=\frac{y+3}{4}=\frac{z-6}{-9}=\lambda$ and $Q(2,4,-1)$
Any random point on the line will be given by $P(\lambda-5,4 \lambda-3,-9 \lambda+6)$
Since $P Q=7 \Rightarrow \sqrt{(\lambda-7)^2+(4 \lambda-7)^2+(-9 \lambda+7)^2}=7$
$\Rightarrow 98\left(\lambda^2-2 \lambda+1\right)=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=1$
Hence, the required point is $P(-4,1,-3)$
The equation of line PQ is $\frac{x+4}{6}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z+3}{2}$ or $\frac{x-2}{6}=\frac{y-4}{3}=\frac{z+1}{2}$

questions.q: Find the equation of the line passing through the point of intersection of the lines $\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-2}{3}$ and $\frac{\mathrm{x}-1}{0}=\frac{\mathrm{y}}{-3}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-7}{2}$ and perpendicular to these given lines.
questions.solution:
$l_1: \frac{x}{1}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{3}=\lambda ; l_2: \frac{x-1}{0}=\frac{y}{-3}=\frac{z-7}{2}=\mu$
any point on $l_1$ is $(\lambda, 2 \lambda+1,3 \lambda+2)$ \& any point on $l_2$ is $(1,-3 \mu, 2 \mu+7)$
If $l_1$ and $l_2$ intersect,
$\lambda=1,2 \lambda+1=-3 \mu \text { and } 3 \lambda+2=2 \mu+7 \Rightarrow \lambda=1 \text { and } \mu=-1$
Point of intersection of $l_1$ and $l_2$ is $(1,3,5)$.
Let d.r.'s of required line be $\langle a, b, c\rangle$. Then,
$a+2 b+3 c=0 \text { and }-3 b+2 c=0 \Rightarrow \frac{a}{13}=\frac{b}{-2}=\frac{c}{-3}$
Required equation of line is $\frac{x-1}{13}=\frac{y-3}{-2}=\frac{z-5}{-3}$

questions.solution:
The standard form of the equation of the line is $\frac{x-4}{-2}=\frac{y}{6}=\frac{z-1}{-3}$

Let foot of the perpendicular from the point $A(2,3,-8)$ to the given line be $B(-2 \lambda+4,6 \lambda,-3 \lambda+1)$
D-ratios of AB is: $-2 \lambda+2,6 \lambda-3,-3 \lambda+9$
As $A B$ is perpendicular to the given line: $-2(-2 \lambda+2)+6(6 \lambda-3)-3(-3 \lambda+9)=0$
$\Rightarrow \lambda=1$
$\therefore$ Foot of the perpendicular is: $B(2,6,-2)$
Perpendicular distance $=\mathrm{AB}=3 \sqrt{5}$

questions.q: Find the vector and the Cartesian equations of a line passing through the point $(1,2,-4)$ and parallel to the line joining the points $\mathrm{A}(3,3,-5)$ and $\mathrm{B}(1,0,-11)$. Hence, find the distance between the two lines.
questions.solution:
Vector equation of required line through $(1,2,-4)$ is
$\vec{r}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{k}}+\lambda(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{k}})$
and cartesian equation: $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{3}=\frac{z+4}{6}$
Equation of line through $\mathrm{A}(3,3,-5)$ and $\mathrm{B}(1,0,-11)$ is
$\vec{r}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}+\mu(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{k}})$
Distance between parallel lines is given by $\mathrm{d}=\frac{\left|\left(\overrightarrow{a_2}-\overrightarrow{a_1}\right) \times \vec{b}\right|}{|\vec{b}|}$
Here $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{k}}, \vec{a}_1=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{k}}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}_2}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\left(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}_2}-\vec{a}_1\right)=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\left(\overrightarrow{a_2}-\overrightarrow{a_1}\right) \times \vec{b}=9 \hat{i}-14 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}$
$\therefore \mathrm{d}=\frac{\sqrt{293}}{7}$

questions.q: Find the equations of the line passing through the points $\mathrm{A}(1,2,3)$ and $\mathrm{B}(3,5,9)$. Hence, find the coordinates of the points on this line which are at a distance of 14 units from point $B$.
questions.solution:
Equation of line AB is $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-2}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-3}{6}$
Let coordinates of required point on AB be $(2 \lambda+1,3 \lambda+2,6 \lambda+3)$ for some $\lambda$
According to Question
$(2 \lambda-2)^2+(3 \lambda-3)^2+(6 \lambda-6)^2=14^2$ gives $\lambda^2-2 \lambda-3=0$
Solving we get $\lambda=3$ and -1
$\therefore$ required points are $(7,11,21)$ and $(-1,-1,-3)$

questions.solution:
Equation of diagonal PR: $\frac{x-4}{8}=\frac{y-2}{2}=\frac{z+6}{11}$
Equation of diagonal QS: $\frac{x-5}{6}=\frac{y+3}{12}=\frac{z-1}{-3}$
General points on $P R \& Q S$ are $(8 k+4,2 k+2,11 k-6)$ and $(6 t+5,12 t-3,-3 t+1)$ for real numbers ' $k$ ' and ' $t$ ' respectively.
For point of intersection of $P R$ and $Q S: 8 k+4=6 t+5,2 k+2=12 t-3$
Solving, we get $k=\frac{1}{2}, t=\frac{1}{2} \therefore$ The point of intersection is $\left(8,3,-\frac{1}{2}\right)$

questions.q: A line $l$ passes through point $(-1,3,-2)$ and is perpendicular to both the lines $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y}{2}=\frac{z}{3}$ and $\frac{x+2}{-3}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z+1}{5}$. Find the vector equation of the line $l$. Hence, obtain its distance from origin.
questions.solution:
Let direction ratios of the required line be $\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{b}, \mathbf{c}$
Since it is perpendicular to the two given lines, $a+2 b+3 c=0 ;-3 a+2 b+5 c=0$
Solving together, $a=4 k, b=-14 k, c=8 k$
$\therefore$ Equation of line is: $\frac{x+1}{4 k}=\frac{y-3}{-14 k}=\frac{z+2}{8 k} \Rightarrow \frac{x+1}{2}=\frac{y-3}{-7}=\frac{z+2}{4}$
Vector equation: $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{r}}=-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}+\lambda(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-7 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}})$
Distance from origin $=\frac{|(-\hat{i}+3 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}) \times(2 \hat{i}-7 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k})|}{|2 \hat{i}-7 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}|}=\frac{|-2 \hat{i}+\hat{k}|}{|2 \hat{i}-7 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}|}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{69}}$ or $\sqrt{\frac{5}{69}}$
